Birds flying 羽 in the daytime 白
Origin unclear.
數飛也。从羽从白。凡習之屬皆从習。

Ideogrammic compound (會意 /会意): 羽 (“wings”) + 日 (“sun”) – to learn to fly, to practice flying.
In the current form, 日 (rì, “sun”) has changed to 白 (bái, “white”), so the present form is 羽 (“wings”) + 白 (“white”).
Alternatively, the original form may have been a phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *ljub): phonetic 彗 (OC *sɢʷeds, *ɢʷeds, *sɢʷids) + semantic 日 (“sun”).
Two general semantic fields are found in the senses: "to flap the wings; to flutter" and "to practice". They are generally considered to be the same word, with the link being "to repeatedly flap the wings (in order to learn to fly)", a sense attested in Liji.
Area word:
* Proto-Sino-Tibetan *sV-ləp (“to learn”): Tibetan སློབ (slob, “to learn”), སློབས (slobs, “exercise; training”); Mizo tlip (“to repeat; to do again; to perfect”),
* Mon-Khmer: Khmer ធ្លាប់ (thlŏəp, “to become accustomed to; to have the habit of; marker of continuous action in the past”); Proto-Mon *le̤p ("to know how to, be skilled in") > Mon လေပ် (lèp, “to be versed in”).

evidence.source: Fudan University Center for Unearthed Documents and Paleography, Chen Jian
evidence.field: discussion of the lower component and graphic history; lines 167–170
evidence.text: Chen argues that oracle-bone 習 is composed of 日 and a 彗 phonetic element, whose shape was later confused with 羽. He cautions that the lower element’s history is more complex than a straightforward change from 日 to 白: Warring States forms occur both with 日 and with a 口/曰-like form, and the latter line leads to the seal form. This conflicts with explanations that derive the seal’s lower 白 directly from 日.
evidence.title: 陳劍：“〖日羽〗”形來源補説

evidence.text: The entry presents oracle forms and Warring States, seal, clerical, regular, and simplified forms. Its analysis reads the oracle graph as 日 plus 彗, with 彗 phonetic and 日 semantic, proposing ‘dry in the sun’ as the original meaning. It reports oracle-bone examples used for ‘袭’ or ‘重’ and later learning-related uses. It also reports no bronze inscriptions for 習, and says that by the Warring States period the 彗 and 羽 shapes had become confused. This is a secondary synthesis, and its semantic account is disputed by other explanations.
evidence.title: 習字形演变字源_汉字「習」_習的甲骨文_習的金文_金文编_甲骨文编

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.text: The database gives the Shuowen account ‘數飛也。从羽从白’ (‘repeated flying; from 羽 and 白’) and separately proposes an oracle graph 日 plus phonetic 彗, whose original sense was sun-drying. It cites oracle-bone ‘習一卜/二卜/三卜’ examples as repeated divinations, and Warring States Guodian slips as evidence for learning-related use: 性自命出 slips 60–61 and 語叢三 slip 10. It treats the bird-practice explanation as an account of later borrowed senses, not a settled account of the earliest graph.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 習

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.text: The database says the element resembling 羽 in the oracle graph is interpreted as 彗 rather than 羽, citing the absence of an oracle 羽 graph and comparison with the 彗 phonetic in the seal form of 雪. In this analysis 彗 supplies sound and 日 meaning; the graph’s original sense is sun-drying. It reports the later Shuowen analysis as 羽 plus 白 and describes those components as graphic confusions by small-seal script. The proposed referents and changes are source interpretations, not independently established merely by resemblance.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析: 羽

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.text: The database identifies oracle-bone examples ‘習一卜’, ‘習二卜’ and ‘習三卜’ in 合集 31672–31674, glossing them as repeated divinations; an alternative explanation attributed to Guo Moruo connects the expressions to groups of divination cracks. editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

items.period: Oracle-bone script style; exact period of the represented form is not specified on the file page
items.caption: This modern digital redraw shows an oracle-script form of 習. The received Shuowen account analyzes 習 as 羽 plus 白 and defines it as repeated flying; a competing analysis reads the oracle form as 日 plus phonetic 彗 and proposes an original sense related to sun-drying. Neither account settles the graph’s original construction.
items.alt: Black oracle-script glyph with a branching upper section and a rounded lower section open at the bottom.
items.selection_reason: The redraw gives readers a clear view of the early graph discussed in competing analyses, while its shape alone cannot identify its components or original meaning.
items.rights: Public domain representation, as stated on the exact Commons file page.

limitations.text: The oracle graph’s components and original meaning remain disputed. The competing analyses do not establish whether the upper shape represents 彗 or 羽, and the lower portion’s history is more complex than a simple 日-to-白 change.
